The live firehose is https://x.com/aaronspradlin. This atlas does not replace it. The public compile is https://aaronspradlin.grok.me. Field notes are the load-bearing science posts. The notebook is a denser 2025–2026 science/method index, including replies. Day-job, Luminaries, emoji-only, and other people’s theories stay on X. A true census still requires the author’s X data export.

The rating this atlas had to answer: B as a compiled research wiki, C as an archive of the science posts. Those are different jobs. This page is the coverage contract — what is ingested, what is curated, and what is refused.

What was wrong with the ingest

The Hubble-tension miss was not a missing URL. It was a bad scan rule. Early compiles preferred GitHub package names and original tweets. They down-ranked replies. H0DN (13 Apr) was a reply to @coreyspowell. The DESI w(z) prediction (30 Apr) was a reply. Today’s t* = 13/33 onset is a reply on the F-bound thread. The 25 Jul 20-part focusing report, the 23 Jul Q_i gate, the 1 Jun “geometry cannot validate itself” traces, the 23 May five-history Genesis Pin filter, and the 4 May Quintom literature thread were original long posts that never became Tmp/TOE folders. Replies that carry equations are now first-class. Month-by-month from:@aaronspradlin scans replace “whatever the last keyword hit.”

Do not filter out replies. A science claim posted under someone else’s thread is still a field note. Do not require a Tmp/TOE folder before an X result can exist. Candidate test: equation, residual, holdout number, video flight log, or walk-back. @grok replies on Aaron’s science threads are first-class: quote them, keep the status URL, do not treat them as someone else’s theory. Live ingest is still out of scope — but a compile that cannot see replies, Grok reviews, or applied telemetry will keep missing cosmology and C3++.

Scan ledger (this compile)
